newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon army lacks authority for curfew - sources.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon army lacks authority for curfew - sources.

text.p: The Lebanese army will help security forces keep order during a planned general strike on Thursday but it has no authority to impose a curfew, security sources said on Wednesday.
"There is no curfew because the army does not have a mandate from the cabinet to take responsibility on its own for security," a source told Reuters.
Interior Minister Michel al-Murr told reporters earlier the army had authority to impose a curfew if necessary to prevent protest demonstrations planned during the strike.
There was no immediate comment from the army.
The sources said soldiers would start deploying on Wednesday afternoon to prevent the demonstrations planned in Beirut and other cities which have been banned by the government.
"The army will support security forces in maintaining stability and implementing the interior ministry's ban on demonstrations," the source said.
"It is expected that army units may deploy on the ground as of this afternoon to provide this support," he added.
